title: This Beetle Shoots Boiling Spray at Its Attackers
sources: MIT News, 30 Apr 2015, 'How bombardier beetles produce their defensive spray': X-ray imaging of living beetles, spray almost at boiling point, made at the moment of use in a reaction chamber, pulsing gives the chamber walls time to cool, rigid reinforced chamber. https://news.mit.edu/2015/how-bombardier-beetles-produce-defensive-spray-0430

National Geographic, 'How this beetle creates 500 explosions per second in its bum': spray around 100 degrees Celsius, 368 to 735 pulses per second, reservoir of hydrogen peroxide and hydroquinones, reaction chamber with enzymes, pulsing lets the chamber cool. https://www.nationalgeographic.com/science/article/how-this-beetle-creates-500-explosions-per-second-in-its-bum

NBC News, 'X-rays reveal secrets of bombardier beetle's machine gun bum': up to 500 pulses per second, boiling-hot mixture. https://www.nbcnews.com/science/weird-science/x-rays-reveal-secrets-bombardier-beetles-machine-gun-bum-n351341
Science Friday, 'How the Bombardier Beetle Packs Its Punch': spray at 212 F (100 C). https://www.sciencefriday.com/articles/picture-of-the-week-bombardier-beetle/
Arndt, Moore, Lee and Ortiz 2015, Science, 'Mechanistic origins of bombardier beetle explosion-induced defensive spray pulsation', doi 10.1126/science.1261166

EurekAlert / MIT press release 821988 on the 2015 Science study: reaction chamber, precursors give off intense heat almost to boiling, vapor, pressure expels it in a jet, irritating liquid made at the instant of use, rigid reinforced chamber, pulsing may give the walls time to cool. https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/821988
